Drought tolerance is a physiological and ecological disposition, not a morphological quality. PATO_0000515 'tolerant to' would need drought as its second term, and drought is in none of our ontologies.
'Feeding roots' names a kind of root by its function, not a quality, and PO has no feeder-root class. The group also mixes in 'raiz grampiforme' (clinging roots), which means something else.

'Micropustuleux' means bearing minute pustules. The 'micro-' gives the size of the pustules, not a different quality, and 'pustuleux' is already a synonym of FLOPO:0991223.

'Thèques frontales' and 'stigma frontal' are position words whose meaning depends on the family and on the face of the flower meant. They are not clearly introrse (FLOPO:0991164) or any PATO position, so a rule would be a guess.
'Petal with a distinct claw' (onglet net) means the petal is clawed. Here 'distinct' means evident, not free.
On palea, lemma, stipule and petiole, 'fissa'/'fendido' means cleft (PATO split, synonym clefted). 'Wood fissile' (splitting easily) is a disposition and should not be grounded by this rule.

definition: A striated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being marked with lines or streaks that are glands on or within its tissue. NOTE: Sibling in sense of FLOPO:0991174 gland-dotted (dots rather than lines); typical of Hypericaceae and Primulaceae-Myrsinoideae.

'A polymorphous species' describes variation within the taxon, not a quality of a plant or part. It is meaningless without the character that varies.

label: free-central
definition: A positional quality inhering in a placenta or its ovules by virtue of their being borne on a central column that rises from the base of a unilocular ovary and is free from the ovary wall. NOTE: Botany-specific (placentation); sibling of FLOPO:0991191 axile and FLOPO:0991192 parietal.

An unobtrusive petal or midvein is one that is not readily noticed, which matches the existing 'obscure'/'indistinct' rules.
This compares the part to an unspecified appendage, and 'appendage' was already rejected as a generic part. The word gives no shape or structure on its own.
'Semi-' weakens cucullate in the same way 'sub-' does, so it is the existing value with the approximate qualifier.

A surface with black dots is punctate. The dots are not always called glands, so the more specific gland-dotted value is not used, and 'black' is the colour of the dots, a second annotation.
Coppicing (resprouting from the base after cutting or fire) is a regeneration response, not a morphological quality. The statements also mix it with habit ('forming coppice').
A petal bearing longitudinal folds is pleated, which is PATO plicate. 'Without folds' is the negated value, and folds at the base of the tube that act as scales may later need a FLOPO part instead.
Very fugitive petals or flowers are shed very early, which is what fugacious means. 'Colour fugitive in drying' is a specimen condition (pattern 06) and must not use this rule.
'Pellucid-dotted' is already a related synonym of FLOPO:0991174: translucent dots that are glands in the leaf tissue.
'Flushed' means tinged with a colour, so this is pink with the approximate qualifier, like 'pinkish'. 'Turning pink-flushed' is a transition between two values and stays in the record.
'Suffused purplish' means tinged purple, so this is purple with the approximate qualifier. 'Beneath' is a surface of the bearer (slot 1).
